recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR core. If misleading missing-Jekyll errors still occur in current IG Publisher releases, investigate the external publisher/tooling repository rather than editing this core source tree.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive Jira asked for a better error when the IG Publisher was run without Jekyll installed, because the observed error misleadingly suggested a temp-directory problem.
initial_application: The Jira comments cite svn 14844, and the git-svn history contains commit 5f3a9115dff2f56f73e97079549ff9ce16ef4376, "GF#16546 - better error if Jekyll fails.", which updated Publisher.java's Jekyll IOException path to log that Jekyll had failed and might not be installed before rethrowing.
additional_context: Commit 56ceb0df08dd72381a4f98f1ea4ac5ea6d139a8b later removed the IG Publisher from this repository with the rationale "Remove IG publisher (it's gone to Maven)". Current source searches find only static Jekyll template/dictionary mentions and no tracked Publisher.java, IGPublisher, org.hl7.fhir.publisher, or Jekyll execution code in this checkout.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No FHIR core source was changed because the requested correction was already applied before the affected tooling left this repository, and any current behavior now belongs to the external publisher/tooling repository.
